author: ddelong
body:
## Problem
[HADOOP-18173](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HADOOP-18173) affects Hadoop 3.3.6. Rather than copying our JARs as one directory in ThinJarUtils, we copy them one at time, and this fails when copying to S3.

## Solution
Tweak the logic. In the case of a single file, the `currentSrcUri` is the path itself. When the specified source is a directory, it doesn't compare against itself because of the calling logic: https://github.com/HubSpot/hadoop/blob/442ae9d40178d49d84b1f86faadc598eadaf8bb7/hadoop-tools/hadoop-aws/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/fs/s3a/impl/CopyFromLocalOperation.java#L217-L220

All directories bypass the `getFinalPath` method, meaning that it can actually be assumed that `src` is not a directory. `source` is a class member that in most cases is a directory, but not always (as described in the above bug report and in our own usage). In the case that `source` and `src` are the same item, we actually want to follow to the last two cases where either the destination is a directory (as is the case for our own `ThinJarUtils`) or the destination is a file to replace.

## Testing
This was tested while setting up a YARN cluster in our environment using S3 for the filesystem.

## Next steps
I would like to upstream this change, but I don't want to delay Vinay's project while we figure that out.

author: infinitewarp
body:
This change enables the `django-axes` middleware for logging failed login attempts and subsequently locking out the user from further login attempts for a specified length of time.

See also:
* https://django-axes.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html
* https://github.com/jazzband/django-axes
* https://pypi.org/project/django-axes/

The UI isn't super pretty now, but I believe we can iterate on that once we get this basic functionality in place. When using the discovery-ui web app, on your Nth failure, you get a simple page that looks like this:

![Screenshot 2024-02-13 at 3 46 01 PM](https://github.com/quipucords/quipucords/assets/1472326/374a88c3-6ec2-4559-b377-c1bd9a59748f)

Repeated failed logins from the `qpc` CLI will also trigger `django-axes` and its lockout functionality, but the CLI doesn't show any additional details like that. It simply says `Error: Unable to log in with provided credentials.` same as the first time you entered bad credentials. We may want to iterate on that as well.

`django-axes` already has APIs *and Django management commands* to reset its failure counters. We may consider writing some docs around them in case some sysadmin accidentally locks themself out and cannot wait for the cooldown to expire.

Those management commands include:
```
[axes]
    axes_list_attempts
    axes_reset
    axes_reset_failure_logs
    axes_reset_ip
    axes_reset_ip_username
    axes_reset_logs
    axes_reset_username
```

author: aarsilv
body:
_Eppo Internal:_
🎟️ **Ticket:** FF-1426 - Adjust bandit logger to separate context by subject and action, and numeric and categorical attributes
🗺️ **Design Review:** [Bandits Engineering Design](https://www.notion.so/eppo/Bandits-Engineering-Design-c5df5b6072b446aa8cacbf54e4d1f9df?pvs=4) (Relevant Section: [1/31 Data Sync](https://www.notion.so/eppo/Bandits-Engineering-Design-c5df5b6072b446aa8cacbf54e4d1f9df?pvs=4#ba69c1a748fc4410814642e801ea3f6c)) 
🗨️ **Slack Thread:** [...are we ok with these property names?...](https://eppo-group.slack.com/archives/C05R6BK5BB9/p1706718580200779)

# Description
To simplify using context to train the bandit, we want to have the SDKs separate out context by numeric (numbers) and categorical (everything else) attributes. We also want these separated by subject and action in the off chance two things are named the same. Therefore, `BanditLogData` has been adjusted to have four fields for use by the customer's logger:
```java
Map<String, Double> subjectNumericAttributes,
Map<String, String> subjectCategoricalAttributes,
Map<String, Double> actionNumericAttributes,
Map<String, String> actionCategoricalAttributes
```
The intention is for the customer to then log these in four different columns in their `bandit_assignments` table.

Updated the tests in `EppoClientTest` to ensure things were sorted out correctly for both `getStringAssignment()` and `logNonBanditAction()`.

author: dsenalik
body:
# New Feature

### Closes #1632 

### ~~Dependent on #1841~~ (merged)
### ~~Dependent on #1854~~ (merged)

### Tripal Version: 4.x

## Description
None of the Tripal 4 fields currently are "clickable" like they were in Tripal 3.
This PR will eventually make this possible.  For example
![2024-02-26_organism-with-link](https://github.com/tripal/tripal/assets/8419404/6e8f2f8d-082f-46bc-9507-460cdaa98a2b)

## Tasks
 - 🙈 ~~Create a new service to generate the entity titles for either one or all records. For example~~
```
    $title_manager = \Drupal::service('tripal.tripal_entity.title');
    $titles = $title_manager->getEntityTitles($datastore, $bundle, $record_id);
```
 ~~This will be a chunk of the code from the publish service, so make it generic enough that the publish service can also use it.~~

 - 🙈 ~~Update the publish service to use the new `tripal.entity_title` service.
 To implement this, make it a child class of the class above.~~
```
use \Drupal\tripal\Services\TripalEntityTitle;
class TripalPublish extends TripalEntityTitle {`
```

 - Abandoned these first two tasks, initial implementation is very slow at ~1.8 seconds to return the url. Generating a title has a large amount of overhead for setup. This was okay for publish, but not for this. Implement an alternative method.

 - [x] Create a new service `tripal.tripal_entity.lookup` to generate either the entity ID or the local URL for a record.
~~This will internally call the `tripal.tripal_entity.title` service.~~

 - [x] Also in this service implement a way to look up a bundle id from a CV term. Such as, if the field links to a gene, we need to know that the bundle name is gene. We can get this from the CV term, which in the field formatter can be retrieved with
```
  $item_settings = $item->getDataDefinition()->getSettings();
  $termIdSpace = $item_settings['termIdSpace'];
  $termAccession = $item_settings['termAccession'];
```
 - [x] Create a function to look up not-null columns in a chado table `getNotNullColumns()`
This will be the only slow step, but we can cache the result with `\Drupal::cache()->set($cache_id, $cache_values);` We only need a single cached set of values for each base table that shows up as a content type, and we don't even need to worry about expiring it after some time because this information won't change.

The reason we want this information is that the chado table and column for the corresponding field is guaranteed to be populated for every entity, because of the non-null constraint.

 - [x] Implement the entity lookup as follows
Select one of the entity tables with a not-null constraint. This insures there is a row for every published entity. Since we know the chado record_id, we can then look for the corresponding entity id with a query similar to this
```
$required_fields = $this->getRequiredFields($bundle_id, $entity_type);
$required_field = array_key_first($required_fields);
$pkey_property_id = 'record_id';  // This assumes all of our fields use this id - so far this is true
$required_property = $required_field . '.' . $pkey_property_id;
$query = \Drupal::entityQuery($entity_type)
      ->condition('type', $bundle_id)
      ->condition($required_property, $record_id, '=')
      ->accessCheck(TRUE);
// The values of the array are always entity ids. The keys will be
// revision ids if the entity supports revision and entity ids if not.
$ids = $query->execute();
```

 - [x] A high level function to simplify code in the  field formatters
~~public function getFieldUrl($displayed_string, $record_id, $item_settings)~~
`$renderable_item = $lookup_manager->getRenderableItem($displayed_string, $values['entity_id']);`

 - [x] Entity lookup is now implemented in the tripalTypes function for each field using a function callback.
```
    // This property will store the Drupal entity ID of the linked chado
    // record, if one exists.
    $properties[] = new ChadoIntStoragePropertyType($entity_type_id, self::$id, 'entity_id', self::$drupal_entity_term, [
      'action' => 'function',
      'drupal_store' => TRUE,
      'namespace' => self::$chadostorage_namespace,
      'function' => self::$drupal_entity_callback,
      'fkey' => self::$object_id,
    ]);
```
The field should then have clickable links, for example
![2024-02-13_issue1632](https://github.com/tripal/tripal/assets/8419404/3076a637-d1cd-45d3-a900-113724808c9d)

 - [x] Handle the cases where the chado base table does not exactly match the drupal table name derived from the content type name, e.g. the `arraydesign` table contact reference is in the table `tripal_entity__array_design_manufacturer` because the content type id is `array_design`
 This also happens for any of the feature table content types, analysis (genome_assembly), etc.

- [x] Figure out URL generation - ~~currently hardcoded because of multi-second time required.~~
The solution was this `$url_object = Url::fromRoute('entity.tripal_entity.canonical', ['tripal_entity' => $entity_id]);` which takes only a few milliseconds.

 - [x] Move the entity lookup to the tripalTypes field functions. The entity will now be looked up when creating content and the formatter will use this value to generate the link.

 - [x] Create tests for the new service

 - [x] Create an update function to update the field tables with the new entity id property

## Testing?
 1. Import all the content type groups
 2. Start adding content, and as you go link to as much as possible. This order works well for content types that have dependencies: Contact, Project, Publication, Protocol, Array Design, Assay, Analysis, Biological Sample, Germplasm Accession, Genetic Marker, Genetic Map, and whatever else seems good.
Note on the Array Design page that the "Manufacturer" is a foreign key to contact, so we should get a link displayed.
Note on the Assay page that the "Operator" is also a foreign key to contact, however the term for this one is NCIT:C48036 which is not a content type, so no link will be added. 🙈 Likewise for Biosource Provider on Biomaterial content type...
 3. Make sure this field works
```
    -   name: analysis_software
        content_type: analysis
        label: Program, Pipeline, Workflow or Method Name
            storage_plugin_settings:
                base_table: analysis
                base_column: program
```

 4. To test the update function, 
   4a. Build a new docker on the 4.x branch
   4b. Add a project and add a contact (without any links)
   4c. Make a link `sitedb=> insert into project_contact (project_id, contact_id) values (1,2);`
   4d. Switch branch `git checkout tv4g1-issue1632-add-field-links-to-entities`
   4e. Run updates `drush updatedb`
   4f. Publish "Project" and "Contact" content types

body:
This PR addresses notes that were identified in NOAA NASA monthly meeting for missing data from AMV, GEO, and SEVIRI and related changes/improvements for the debugging process. 

Changes include: 
- updating atm dictionaries to include additional bufr/prepbufr files which can be inventoried (including the missing amv and geo folders)

- split amv plot by subsensor to split up merged and satwnd by line

- ability to specify work directory for nceplibs calls at command line (allows improved speed for runs since we can download files to lustre instead of contrib) 
- edited scripts to not fail if a satellite name doesn't exist in our dictionary and instead print error message -- this is key to our ability to run the scripts consistently with new satellites getting added to our dataset. if a satellite isn't in the list, it will only related to our ability to match satinfo files
- fixed date string issue which prevented help info showing for -h --help flags for arg help descriptions
- removed superfluous info statements which printed excessive amounts of data to improve speed and allow for easier identification of actual error print outs

author: adrianlizarraga
body:
### Description
Fuses DQ -> Q sequences into a QNN Convert operator if:
- Converting from one qtype to another. Ex: Dequantize(uint8 to float) -> Quantize(float to uint16)
- The DQ and Q operators are not part of another node unit (i.e., standalone)
- The Q operator is the only consumer for the DQ operator.



### Motivation and Context
Allows faster execution of QDQ models with mixed activation types by leveraging the QNN Convert operator, which converts between quantization types. For certain models, this results in inference latency speed-ups of up to 2x (depends on the number of DQ -> Q sequences).

#### Example for Add node unit with 16-bit I/O:

Original:
```
u8 ----> DQ ---> Q ---u16--> Add ---u16-->
                              ^
                              |
u16 --------------------------+
```

After fusing DQ -> Q:
```
u8 ----> Convert ---u16--> Add ---u16-->
                            ^
                            |
u16 ------------------------+
```

author: debarshiray
body:
Currently, the Fedora Packaging Guidelines don't choose sides between absolute and relative symbolic links [1], but RPM does [2,3].  Building the crun RPM with absolute symlinks leads to:
```
  ...
  warning: absolute symlink: /usr/bin/krun -> /usr/bin/crun
  ...
  warning: absolute symlink: /usr/bin/crun-wasm -> /usr/bin/crun
  ...
  RPM build warnings:
    absolute symlink: /usr/bin/krun -> /usr/bin/crun
    absolute symlink: /usr/bin/crun-wasm -> /usr/bin/crun
  ...
```

Given the prevalence of chroot-like environments these days due to bind mounts in containers, relative symbolic links do look like the better alternative, and various prominent parts of the operating system already use them.  Some examples:
  * /etc/localtime -> ../usr/share/zoneinfo/Europe/Prague
  * /etc/mtab -> ../proc/self/mounts
  * /etc/os-release -> ../usr/lib/os-release
  * /usr/bin/dnf -> dnf-3
  * /usr/bin/ghostscript -> /usr/bin/gs
  * /usr/bin/gpg2 -> gpg
  * /usr/bin/python -> ./python3
  * /usr/bin/python3 -> python3.11
  * /usr/bin/qemu-kvm -> qemu-system-x86_64
  * /usr/bin/systemd-resolve -> resolvectl
  * /usr/bin/systemd-umount -> systemd-mount
  * /usr/bin/traceroute6 -> traceroute
  * /usr/bin/unxz -> xz

[1] https://docs.fedoraproject.org/en-US/packaging-guidelines/#_symlinks

[2] https://github.com/rpm-software-management/rpm/issues/668

[3] https://github.com/rpm-software-management/rpm/issues/2419

author: benhoyt
body:
This avoids the 3-lock deadlock described in
https://github.com/canonical/pebble/issues/314. Other goroutines
may be holding the state lock and waiting for the services lock, so
it's problematic to acquire both locks at once. Break that part of the cycle.

We could do this inside serviceForStart/serviceForStop by manually
calling Unlock() sooner, but that's error-prone, so continue using defer,
but have the caller write the task log (which needs the state lock) after
the services lock is released.

This is in preference to the more invasive change in https://github.com/canonical/pebble/pull/356

apiVersion: credentialprovider.d2iq.com/v1alpha1

mirror:

credentialProviderPluginBinDir: /etc/kubernetes/image-credential-provider/

- reads mirror credentials from secret and add its provider configuration in DynamiCredentialsProviderConfig if provided
e.g.
```
apiVersion: credentialprovider.d2iq.com/v1alpha1

mirror:

**What this PR does / why we need it**: Per the issue, this adds a File page Edit menu Uningest/Reingest menu item for tabular files, visible to superusers, that allows clearing ingest errors/removing ingested tab files, and ingesting/reingesting a file (useful if a new Dataverse version may have fixes or if ingest limits change, etc.)

**Which issue(s) this PR closes**:

Closes #10318

**Special notes for your reviewer**:  The PR as is, keeps these as requiring superuser. At QDR, we switched to allowing anyone who has permission to publish the dataset to uningest/reingest via API/UI. For QDR, that means curators can use these options whereas in a non-curated/self-publication setup it would allow anyone to do this in their draft datasets. If that's desired, the permission changes can be added to this PR.

**Suggestions on how to test this**: Go to the file page and try the uningest/reingest options on a tabular file. Verify that for a file where ingest has failed, that uningest clears the error and that for one where ingest succeeded, the .tab version is removed. Verify that reingest does an ingest (and fails or succeeds as the initial ingest did).

**Does this PR introduce a user interface change? If mockups are available, please link/include them here**: single entry (uningest or reingest) in the File page Edit menu, visible for superusers.
